Cut a numeric vector into groups

Source: R/cut.R
cut.Rd

Group numeric values using quantiles, equal widths, or chosen cutpoints:

  • cut_quantile() (xtile()): Create n quantile groups, following Stata's xtile.

  • cut_length(): Create n intervals of equal length. Stata has no equal-width command (egen cut(), group() is not equal-width).

  • cut_breaks(): Cut at given cutpoints, like egen cut(), at().

Usage

cut_quantile(
  x,
  n = 4,
  labels = NULL,
  method = c("quantile", "rank"),
  wt = NULL
)

xtile(x, n = 4, labels = NULL, method = c("quantile", "rank"), wt = NULL)

cut_length(x, n = 4, labels = NULL)

cut_breaks(x, breaks = NULL, labels = NULL, right = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector. cut_quantile() also accepts logical vectors, treated as 0/1. SPSS user-missing codes and ranges are omitted. Convert integer64 inputs and cutpoints explicitly to ordinary numeric values first.

n

Number of groups or intervals, as a positive integer. Defaults to 4.

labels

NULL (default) creates labels; FALSE returns integer codes. Supply a character vector for custom labels, one per effective group. For cut_quantile(), grouped data masks default to integer codes, and TRUE explicitly requests labels.

method

For cut_quantile(), quantile boundaries ("quantile", the default) or balanced rank groups ("rank", with no Stata counterpart). Rank groups may split ties, breaking them by original position. They differ in size by at most one; earlier groups get extra rows.

wt

Optional finite, non-negative weights for cut_quantile(), one per element of x or a scalar recycled to its length, like Stata's xtile ... [aweight = w]. Cutpoints follow Stata's weighted percentile rule. Zero-weight rows do not enter cutpoint estimation but still receive codes; elements with a missing weight get a missing code. Not available with method = "rank".

breaks

Numeric cutpoints for cut_breaks(). The observed minimum and maximum are added when values lie beyond the breaks. NULL uses the observed median as an interior cutpoint. A single number supplies one interior cutpoint, rather than the number of intervals.

right

For cut_breaks(), if FALSE (default), intervals are closed on the left (a <= x < b), as in Stata's egen cut(); the last interval also includes its upper end. If TRUE, they are closed on the right (a < x <= b), and the first interval also includes its lower end, as in base::cut() with include.lowest = TRUE.

Value

An ordered factor, or integer interval codes when labels = FALSE or when cut_quantile() runs in a grouped data mask with default labels. Results have the length and order of x; missing inputs and missing weights give missing codes. All-missing inputs are rejected. Empty inputs are rejected by cut_quantile() and cut_length(); cut_breaks(numeric(), breaks = 50) returns an empty ordered factor, or an empty integer vector with labels = FALSE.

Details

Quantile and rank groups

In quantile mode, cut_quantile() uses Stata's percentiles at 1/n, 2/n, ... (see summ()). Each value joins the first group whose cutpoint is at least that value. Equal values stay together; different values may share a group. Ties can leave empty groups, whose codes are skipped (for example 1, 3, 4), with a warning. Factor levels contain only occupied groups.

Rank mode omits missing values while ranking and restores their missing output positions afterward. If n exceeds the observed count, it warns and uses one group per observation.

Labels and grouped use

Quantile labels describe contiguous intervals, such as "[0,0]" and "(0,1]"; rank labels run from "1" to the effective group count. Custom labels must match the effective number of groups. Interval labels always use a decimal point, regardless of options(OutDec), to avoid ambiguity with commas.

Inside grouped dplyr::mutate(), each group has its own cutpoints and labels. Because those labels cannot be combined, cut_quantile() defaults to integer codes, like Stata's xtile, by(); labels = TRUE requests labels explicitly. cut_length() and cut_breaks() retain factor output in grouped data masks. For these functions, supply character labels or use FALSE for integer codes.

Limits and interval endpoints

cut_quantile() rejects empty and all-missing inputs; constants are allowed only in rank mode. cut_length() and cut_breaks() reject constants and all-missing inputs. Equal-width intervals also require finite values.

cut_breaks() extends end intervals to the observed range. Stata's egen cut(), at() instead leaves values outside the breaks, including values at the last break, missing.

See also

Other variable generation functions: as_dummy(), panel, row_egen, stata_recode(), std()

Examples

cut_quantile(1:20)
#>  [1] [1,5.5]     [1,5.5]     [1,5.5]     [1,5.5]     [1,5.5]     (5.5,10.5] 
#>  [7] (5.5,10.5]  (5.5,10.5]  (5.5,10.5]  (5.5,10.5]  (10.5,15.5] (10.5,15.5]
#> [13] (10.5,15.5] (10.5,15.5] (10.5,15.5] (15.5,20]   (15.5,20]   (15.5,20]  
#> [19] (15.5,20]   (15.5,20]  
#> Levels: [1,5.5] < (5.5,10.5] < (10.5,15.5] < (15.5,20]

cut_length(1:20)
#>  [1] [1,5.75)    [1,5.75)    [1,5.75)    [1,5.75)    [1,5.75)    [5.75,10.5)
#>  [7] [5.75,10.5) [5.75,10.5) [5.75,10.5) [5.75,10.5) [10.5,15.2) [10.5,15.2)
#> [13] [10.5,15.2) [10.5,15.2) [10.5,15.2) [15.2,20]   [15.2,20]   [15.2,20]  
#> [19] [15.2,20]   [15.2,20]  
#> Levels: [1,5.75) < [5.75,10.5) < [10.5,15.2) < [15.2,20]

cut_breaks(1:20, breaks = c(5, 15))
#>  [1] [1,5)   [1,5)   [1,5)   [1,5)   [5,15)  [5,15)  [5,15)  [5,15)  [5,15) 
#> [10] [5,15)  [5,15)  [5,15)  [5,15)  [5,15)  [15,20] [15,20] [15,20] [15,20]
#> [19] [15,20] [15,20]
#> Levels: [1,5) < [5,15) < [15,20]

cut_breaks(1:20, breaks = 10)
#>  [1] [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10)  [1,10) 
#> [10] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20] [10,20]
#> [19] [10,20] [10,20]
#> Levels: [1,10) < [10,20]
